# Coding Guidelines

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS - Current state

### 1. Use strict, explicitly typed PHP

PHP files declare strict types and methods use parameter and return types, reducing implicit coercion across application boundaries (`app/Models/User.php`, `app/Actions/SystemErrorAlert/UpsertSystemErrorAlert.php`). PHPStan enforces the type model through `phpstan.neon` and `composer test`.

### 2. Keep application behavior in focused classes

Routes delegate to controllers or Livewire components, while mutations and workflows live in dedicated Action or Brain Action classes (`routes/search.php`, `app/Brain/Users/Actions/CreateUserAction.php`, `app/Actions/Media/CreateMedia.php`). Architectural tests in `tests/Unit/ArchTest.php` and mirrored dedicated tests enforce class boundaries.

### 3. Represent finite domain values with enums

User types, permissions, queue names, alert states, and execution states use PHP enums rather than unstructured literals (`app/Enums/TypeUsers.php`, `app/Enums/Queues.php`, `app/Enums/SystemErrorAlertStatuses.php`). Models cast persisted integer values back to their enum types.

### 4. Test each behavior-bearing class in its matching suite

Production paths are mirrored by dedicated Pest files, such as `app/Brain/Users/Actions/CreateUserAction.php` and `tests/Brain/Users/Actions/CreateUserActionTest.php`. `composer test` runs linting, static analysis, type coverage, coverage, and parallel Pest tests.

### 5. Apply repository formatting automatically

PHP formatting is defined by `pint.json`, text defaults by `.editorconfig`, and frontend formatting by Prettier configuration in `package.json`. Husky hooks under `.husky/` run repository checks before changes leave the workstation.
